summary: Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University (~1925–1928), where he later held a post (~1949–1973), before serving as professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1973–1983).
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1942–1948) and later served as professor emeritus there (~1988–2010).

Ryoshun Okubo (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies. After studying at Waseda University (~1973–1982), he became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism there (~2006) and served as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007).
Ryoso Matsushita works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Daishun Ueyama and held a post as lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Ryota Nakamura specializes in Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was a doctoral student and graduate student researcher at Toyo University and a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Ryotai Hatai (1883–1974) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at Kyoto University (1929–1943) and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1954–1974).

Ryudo Fujii specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson, and held posts at JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Taga (born 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar. After studying at Rissho University (~1953–1955), he held posts there as lecturer (attested 1961), associate professor (attested 1972), professor (attested 1983), and president (~1992–1995).

Ryugen Tanemura (born 1968) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and Taisho University (attested 2014–2018).

Ryuichi Abe (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Keio, SAIS, and Columbia, serving as professor at Columbia (~1996–2005) before becoming Edwin O. Reischauer Institute Professor at Harvard University (~2005).

Ryuichi Kogachi (born 1970) is a Sinologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1989–1999) and held posts at the Kyoto University Research Centre for the Cultural Sciences (~2001) and Kyoto University (~2001–2007; associate professor ~2007).

Ryujo Yamada (1895–1979) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi, holding posts at Ryukoku University (~1925–1946) and Tohoku University (~1946–1958; professor emeritus ~1958–1979).

Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as professor emeritus at Taisho University (attested 2014) and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014).
Ryusei Keira specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies under supervisor Tom J. F. Tillemans at the University of Lausanne, finishing his thesis by 2003.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1958) and held posts at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Center (attested 1962) and Kyoto Women's University (professor, attested 1982).
Ryusho Onami (born 1926) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Taishun Mibu and held a post as lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1985).

Ryuta Kikutani works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as a specialist researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center and Graduate School of Letters (attested 2020).

Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947) is an Indologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo and at the University of Marburg (~1973–1979) under Wilhelm Rau and others, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1986–2012).
Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1916, he studied under Chishu Kitagawa and traditional teacher Chijo Kitagawa.
Ryōkei Kaginushi (1926–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters at Otani University (attested 1978 and 1987–1993).
